{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient / Customer)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement (Exhibit 10.14), dated 5 February  
**Position:** We represent the Customer.

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is unusually favourable to us in several respects: the arrangement is expressly non-exclusive, there is no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum commitment, no liquidated damages or exit penalty, no non-solicitation binding us, and no Vendor audit right over our books or systems. Vendor-side indemnification (Section 10(a), with procedure at Section 11) and the express performance warranties (Section 9(b), running throughout the Term) meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline.

The defects are concentrated in four areas, three of them critical or high:

- **No liability cap anywhere in the Agreement.** Section 7 excludes consequential damages only. Our direct liability is unlimited, which fails even the fallback. This is the single most material open point.
- **No intellectual property or ownership article.** Nothing confirms that we retain rights in our Content, Properties and the Requests/visitor data flowing to Kubient, and nothing addresses ownership of the "deliverables" the Vendor warrants. Helpfully, nothing assigns our IP away either, so this is a gap rather than an adverse allocation.
- **Licence grant is expressly "revocable" and runs to "Customer" alone.** As drafted the Vendor could withdraw platform access at discretion mid-term, and our affiliates and contractors are not covered. This is walk-away territory under the licence rule.
- **Exit mechanics are thin.** No transition assistance or data-return obligation (each party may simply "destroy" the other's Confidential Information), a 90-day notice requirement to exit a renewal term, and no Vendor insurance of any kind despite the Vendor collecting and storing visitor information.

Three findings are marked **needs review**: our substantive analysis concludes each is compliant (termination for convenience at the fallback; audit and non-solicitation at the preferred position, by absence), but automated verification did not confirm them and they should be signed off before we send comments.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | Preamble (Section 7) | No monetary cap anywhere; direct liability unlimited both ways. Fails the fallback. Redline adds a mutual cap measured on amounts paid or payable between the Parties over the preceding 12 months with a USD 1,000,000 floor, uncapped Excluded Claims, and revenue-share amounts under Section 5 excluded from the cap. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble | No IP/ownership article. Section 14(b) (marks) and Section 9(c)(i) (our Content warranty) are not usable substitutes. Redline inserts a short ownership section; nothing currently assigns our IP to the Vendor, so not walk-away. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 10(a), 11, 9(b)) | Genuine Vendor-side indemnity covering third-party Claims, IP infringement (via Sections 10(a)(i)–(ii), (iv) and the Section 9(b)(i) non-infringement warranty), data breach and unlawful conduct; procedure at Section 11; no sub-cap. At the preferred position. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble (¶2; cf. ¶4(c)(ii), p0072) | Grant is "revocable" without qualification and runs to "Customer" only. Redline extends the grant to our affiliates and contractors and confines revocation to termination under paragraph 4; "non-transferable" left carved back to the assignment clause. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble (p0072) | We may assign to an affiliate, asset purchaser or merger successor without consent; no change-of-control trigger anywhere. Exceeds the fallback. Noted only: symmetry lets the Vendor do likewise, and there is no bar on assignment to a competitor. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) | Expressly non-exclusive; we remain free to offer Inventory via other agents or sell to third parties. Preferred position. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) | No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction on us. Preferred position. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Preamble (p0016, p0023) | No liquidated damages, penalty or exit fee. Vendor's entitlement to revenue generated during the 90-day notice period is earned revenue share, not a termination charge. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** | Preamble (¶4(a); Section 5) | Our analysis: compliant at the fallback — ¶4(a) grants "Either Party" (and so us, per the defined terms) a no-cause right on 90 days' notice, 1-year Initial Term with 1-year renewals, no exit fee. Automated check failed on string-matching only (¶4(a) does not use the word "Customer"). Requires sign-off; no redline proposed. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | Preamble (¶4(a)) | Renewal length is fine (successive 1-year terms), but the only exit requires 90 days' notice, exceeding the 60-day fallback ceiling. Redline shortens our notice to 30 days (60 acceptable as fallback), leaving the Vendor at 90. No price-uplift language exists, so the CPI/3% cap is not engaged. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | Preamble (Section 4(c), p0019–p0022) | Vendor need only cease Services; licence is revoked; each party may "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at its own election. No usable-format data return, no assistance period, no deletion certification. Redline inserts a new Section 4(c)(v): up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable export within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter (90 days' assistance offered as fallback). |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | Preamble (Section 14(a)) | Delaware law (accepted fallback) with exclusive venue in New York state and federal courts (preferred forum). Noted: Section 8 also provides for AAA arbitration, which sits awkwardly with exclusive court venue — a clean-up point, not a deviation. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | Preamble (Section 9(b), ¶4(a), Section 13) | Express Vendor warranties on material performance, freedom from utility-affecting errors, no malicious code and legal compliance, running "now and throughout the Term" (minimum one year). Section 13 disclaimer is expressly subject to the stated warranties. No sole-remedy language, so we retain all remedies — we will not introduce a repair/replace/refund clause that would cap recovery. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Needs review** | Preamble | Our analysis: no Vendor audit, inspection, verification or record-keeping right exists, leaving our audit exposure at nil — at least as favourable as the preferred position. Automated frequency check fails by construction (no clause to cap). Requires sign-off; no redline, since drafting limits would first have to create the right. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Needs review** | Preamble (p0066) | Our analysis: no non-solicit, no-poach or no-hire covenant binds either party; the independent-contractor clause imposes none. Absence is the preferred outcome for us. Both deterministic checks fail by construction. Requires sign-off; no redline. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 1, 5) | No MFN or price/terms-matching obligation on us; revenue share is set by Exhibit. Preferred position. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 1, 5, 13) | Pure revenue share on actual activity; no committed spend, shortfall charge or volume cap. Section 13 only disclaims guaranteed Vendor revenue. Preferred position. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 14) | No insurance obligation anywhere, despite the Vendor collecting, maintaining and storing visitor information (Section 9(b)(iii)). Redline inserts a new Section 14(j): CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request (fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points our playbook treats as walk-away or approaching walk-away. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **Unlimited direct liability (LOL-CAP, critical).** The absence of any monetary cap fails even the fallback and leaves our exposure open-ended. A mutual cap with uncapped Excluded Claims is required.
2. **Revocable licence with no affiliate or contractor coverage (LICENSE, high).** The combination of an unqualified right of revocation and a grant running to "Customer" alone is the walk-away case under this rule; revocation must be confined to termination under paragraph 4.
3. **No Vendor insurance where the Vendor processes personal data (INSURANCE).** The rule treats a data-processing vendor carrying no coverage as walk-away territory, notwithstanding the low severity rating; at minimum we need the fallback E&O and cyber limits.
4. **Unilateral right to destroy our information on exit (TRANSITION).** Section 4(c) permits the Vendor to elect destruction with no obligation to return or export our data in usable form — this approaches the walk-away outcome and must be paired with a return/export and certified-deletion mechanic.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Clear the three needs-review findings (T4C, AUDIT, NOSOLICIT).** Our substantive view is that each is compliant — the first at the fallback, the latter two at the preferred position by virtue of absence — but automated verification did not confirm them and the failures appear to be artifacts of keyword matching against clauses that either use "Either Party" or do not exist. Please confirm before the markup leaves the building.
2. **Issue the redline covering the five actionable items:** the mutual liability cap in Section 7; a new IP/Customer Data ownership section; the licence-grant amendments; the new Section 4(c)(v) transition and data-return subparagraph; the shortened 30-day non-renewal notice; and the new Section 14(j) insurance provision.
3. **Sequence the negotiation.** The cap and the licence revocation are the priority asks and should be presented as conditions of signature. Ownership, transition and insurance are drafting gaps rather than adverse allocations and should land with limited resistance, with the stated fallbacks (licence-back in lieu of assignment; 90 days' transition assistance; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) available as landing zones.
4. **Raise the dispute-resolution inconsistency as a clean-up point.** Section 14(a) gives exclusive court venue in New York while Section 8 provides for AAA arbitration. This is not a deviation and not walk-away, but we should ask which mechanism governs.
5. **Flag one contingency for the deal team.** Several findings rest on the Section 5 revenue-share model, under which the Vendor pays us and we prepay nothing. If the commercial model moves to a prepaid or subscription-fee basis, the absent pro-rata refund mechanic becomes live and the termination, renewal and liability-cap measurement should be re-run against the revised fee clause. Likewise, Section 1 defines Services by Exhibit and Section 5 lets Exhibits override the default fee mechanics — if a future Exhibit introduces Customer-side reporting or a fee true-up, we should then negotiate the preferred audit limits (fallback: 15 days' notice / 10% underpayment threshold).
"}
